instruction_control.authority_verification: required bootstrap files were read and their blobs matched the manifest-bound current control tuple before this bounded semantic slice

deduplication.reason: The prior mechanism protects semantic payload while a current reachable in-domain lineage remains. This slice covers the harder failure where the same authority can erase or rewind every recovery-visible witness in that rollback-coupled durability domain, including current copies and retaining refs.

tested_scope.failure_model: All recovery-visible durable state is inside one rollback-coupled authority domain. That authority can rewind, delete, or recreate the whole domain after an advancement, and the role-local volatile memory is lost. Recovery receives only observations remaining inside that same domain.
excluded_claims: No claim is made about a second durability service/provider because none was verified in this slice.
No claim is made that current O lacks or has such a second domain; current O presence was not reassessed in this bounded slice.
No claim is made beyond whole-domain erasure plus local-memory-loss scope.

requirements.R1_no_fabricated_advancement: Recovery must never claim S1 in a history where S1 never occurred.
requirements.R2_positive_last_state_recovery: After a real S1 advancement followed by modeled whole-domain erasure, recovery must recover S1 rather than merely fail closed.

indistinguishable_histories.H0: System remains at S0 and never advances to S1.
indistinguishable_histories.H1: System advances to S1 and records witness W1, then the same rollback-coupled authority erases or rewinds every in-domain trace of S1/W1 so the recovery-visible observation is identical to H0.
indistinguishable_histories.observation_equivalence: By construction, the recovery algorithm receives the same allowed observation in H0 and H1.

result.theorem: No recovery action based only on the modeled same-domain observation can satisfy both R1 and R2 for H0 and H1. Positive recovery therefore requires at least one witness whose authority/durability is outside the rollback-coupled domain, or an equivalent non-erasable monotonic authority assumption. Fail-closed preserves R1 but does not satisfy positive recovery R2.
result.phase1_gate_effect: This is a blocker/necessity result, not an accepted dependency-elimination mechanism. A concrete second-domain witness must still be authority-verifiably demonstrated under zero Work, zero finite remaining quota, and zero incremental monetary cost before it can count toward Phase-1 closure.

continuation: Next invocation, from this exact role-local checkpoint and the latest authority-valid controls, verify exactly one candidate second durability domain against Phase-1 gates: it must lie outside repository rollback authority for the modeled failure, provide a monotonic/non-erasable witness sufficient to distinguish H0 from H1, require zero Work/protected-primary/manual-user execution, consume no finite remaining monthly/trial/paid quota, and add zero monetary cost. If no authority-verifiable candidate is available in that one bounded slice, persist the exact blocker and test whether fail-closed is the only admissible behavior for that dependency under the currently exposed surfaces.
